instruction: Please help me modify VS Code settings to hide all ".git" folders in the explorer view.

metadata.explanation: Task requires hiding .git folders in VS Code explorer view by modifying settings.json. Similar to original task but targets .git folders instead of __pycache__. Uses existing check_json_settings metric to verify the files.exclude setting contains **/.git: true.

llm_judge_reasons: The check_json_settings metric uses exact dictionary equality checking (actual_value != value at vscode.py:74), which will fail if the user already has other patterns in files.exclude
Instruction requires adding '**/.git': true to files.exclude (subset match), but evaluator checks if files.exclude exactly equals {'**/.git': true} (exact match)
If settings.json already contains other exclude patterns like '__pycache__' or '.DS_Store', the evaluator will incorrectly return 0.0 even though the task was completed correctly
The metric does not check for the presence of the specific pattern within files.exclude, only that the entire files.exclude value matches exactly
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Modify check_json_settings to support nested key checking: instead of checking if data['files.exclude'] == {'**/.git': true}, check if data.get('files.exclude', {}).get('**/.git') == true
Alternative: Create a new metric function that checks if a specific key-value pair exists within a nested dictionary, rather than requiring exact match of the entire nested structure
Alternative: Change the expected value to be more flexible, checking only that '**/.git' is present in files.exclude with value true, allowing other patterns to coexist
